newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine Airlines says to sack strikers Nov 1.
newsitem.headline: Philippine Airlines says to sack strikers Nov 1.

text.p: Philippine Airlines (PAL) on Thursday told thousands of striking employees they would be out of a job if they did not return to work by tomorrow.
"PAL management has advised striking personnel to return to work not later than Friday, November 1, or be deemed terminated from the company," the national carrier said in a statement.
The strike, launched on Wednesday after President Fidel Ramos rejected a union request to intervene, has so far forced PAL to cancel seven international and 28 domestic flights.
The airline said 11 international and 10 domestic flights had taken off from Manila on Thursday morning.
Thousands of passengers have been affected by the dispute, which mainly involves maintenance workers and airport ground staff, members of the 9,000-strong PAL Employees Association (PALEA).
The Department of Labour set up talks between the two sides on Thursday and these were continuing, PAL officials said.
PALEA said it was determined to fight to the end in the dispute over pay and conditions.
"Our jobs here are at stake, the future of our families. We are being pushed to the wall," the union's national organiser, Jose Penas, told Reuters.
The union had earlier urged President Ramos to intervene in the long-running dispute to avert a potentially embarrassing strike ahead of next month's APEC summit.
But Ramos, who has said the Philippines must put on its "best face" for the November 25 Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, declined, saying he was not a labour arbiter.
The strike was PAL's third in two years. PALEA struck twice in 1994, the first lasting a day and the second nine days.

PALEA and two other airline unions want a new wage package worth 3.2 billion pesos ($121 million) over the next two years. PAL has rejected this and instead offered to sell PAL shares worth 477 million pesos ($18.15 million) at five pesos (19 cents) per share to its employees.

The airline, hit by high operating costs and stiff competition, has lost money heavily in the last several years and said it expects its net loss to be more than one billion pesos ($38 million) in its current fiscal year.
